summary.headline: Birla Corp FY26 volume grew about 4% to a record with EBITDA near INR800 crore for the year and about INR1,000 crore in Q4, with FY27 volume guided only as mid-single-digit growth.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year with some plant operating setbacks that were overcome, delivering around 4% volume growth and a record volume from existing capacity. Q4 EBITDA was close to INR1,000 crore, with blended cement share rising from 82% to 88% and trade share from 70% to 77% over the year. Management is now building capacity from 21.5 to 27.5 million tonnes by FY29 at a capex of about INR4,753 crore including GST, and is guiding FY27 capex of INR900 crore. Management flagged that FY27 cost per tonne will rise by INR150-175 from Q1 on packaging and fuel, and declined to give EBITDA or volume guidance beyond broad directional statements.

segments.name: Cement (blended and premium)
segments.commentary: Blended cement at 88% and trade share at 77% of volumes in FY26; premium share about 63% per analyst read-back, with management aiming to move progressively towards near 100% blended. Perfect Plus is the flagship premium brand, now present across North and Central India.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete (RMC)
segments.commentary: Progress described as slow but steady; a fifth RMC plant in Uttar Pradesh is due soon, marketed under Perfect Plus. Management does not want to scale aggressively given receivable and recovery risks.

segments.name: Construction chemicals and wall putty
segments.commentary: Chemicals seen as a brand extension with a supply chain model being revamped and scale-up planned for the coming year; wall putty not being pursued aggressively as it is highly price-driven. Management said chemicals will never be a huge number and capex is light.

segments.name: Jute
segments.commentary: Management said the jute business had a turnaround-year setback due to abnormal raw jute prices and import disruptions from Bangladesh, with several mills shut or on reduced days. Management ruled out a strategic investor and is hoping for policy support after the change of government in West Bengal.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume expected to grow mid-single digit, not a specific number; analyst's 20 million tonnes figure was not confirmed by management.
FY27 cost per tonne to rise by INR150-175 from Q1, mainly packaging and fuel cost.
FY27 capex of about INR900 crore; total capex for expansion from 21.5 to 27.5 million tonnes by FY29 is about INR4,753 crore including GST (about INR4,300 crore net of GST).
No specific EBITDA guidance; management expects FY27 EBITDA in a similar range to FY26.
Incentive income expected to rise to about INR130 crore in FY27 with Kundanganj coming on stream; Maharashtra incentive annual run-rate about INR90-95 crore.
Debt to rise during capex cycle; peak net debt expected around INR4,000 crore, with debt to EBITDA not expected to exceed 2.5x.
capex_capacity: Capacity to rise from 21.5 to 27.5 million tonnes by FY29, with Maihar Line-II and linked grinding units (including Eastern UP around Prayagraj) in the plan; all additions in FY29.
Kundanganj 1.4 million tonne unit started, along with a third line; Prayagraj and Gaya Phase 1 each 1.4 million tonnes, expected in Q3-Q4 FY28.
Bikram coal block: annual capacity about 3.6 lakh tonnes, about 1.2 lakh tonnes expected in FY27, full capacity from FY28; landed cost INR1.00-1.05 per million kcal vs domestic coal about INR1.45.
Brahampuri coal block not being pursued actively as bid capacity is much lower than stated; Marki Barka expected to start by FY29 subject to regulatory issues.

Renewable energy at 31% of power consumption, targeted at 37-38% in FY27-28; an additional 25-30 MW of solar and hybrid/WHR capacity planned over 1-2 years. Kcal about 700-710 per tonne of clinker, varying by plant.
demand_pricing: Management sees rising non-trade and OPC demand in many markets but says it is not chasing OPC; focus remains blended and premium cement.
Premium share and blended share expected to rise, but management would not commit to reaching 100% blended or to a timeline; slippage possible quarter to quarter.
Price hike of about INR50 per tonne taken in April, per analyst read-back of CNBC comments; not confirmed in call beyond the cost increase commentary.
Management says competitors who added capacity in UP are grinding OPC, which it will not do even with incentives; it views its high utilisation as a reason it is not under pressure to add volume.
Domestic fuel prices rising as cement players switch from imported fuel; imported fuel share about 30% of mix.

qa_highlights.question: Growth plans, capacity expansion and premium positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: No major capacity expansion beyond Maihar Line-II and linked grinding units; target 27.5 million tonnes by FY29, with focus on blended and premium cement and no acquisitions currently.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation and cost levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of about INR4,000-4,500 crore underway, with most internal accruals going to capex, so debt will rise; debt to EBITDA to stay below 2.5x. Bikram coal is the main cost lever from next year.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume, price hike, cost increase and capex reconfirmation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the analyst: it said mid-single-digit volume growth, not a specific 20 million tonnes; cost per tonne to rise INR150-175 from Q1; FY27 capex INR900 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital tighten and what is net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel inventory was built deliberately at year-end due to coal price and geopolitical concerns; net debt about INR2,100 crore, peak net debt expected around INR4,000 crore in this capex cycle; interest cost hard to estimate as term loans are linked to floating benchmarks.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Maharashtra incentive of about INR500 crore receivable not yet realised, plus higher working capital from fuel inventory; realisation expected from FY27.

qa_highlights.question: RMC and construction chemicals plans and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: RMC is a brand extension, with a fifth UP plant soon; chemicals to scale up with revamped supply chain but remain small; capex light.

qa_highlights.question: Incentives in FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 incentive income about INR140 crore total, of which about INR90 crore for earlier years and about INR48-50 crore for the current year; FY27 expected around INR130 crore.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow weakness: INR500 crore incentive receivable and fuel inventory build need to unwind in FY27.
Net debt rising toward about INR4,000 crore peak during the capex cycle; floating-rate term loans make interest cost hard to forecast.
Cost pressure of INR150-175 per tonne from Q1 FY27 from packaging and fuel, with domestic fuel prices also rising.
Execution risk on Kundanganj ramp-up, Prayagraj and Gaya units in FY28, and Maihar Line-II in FY29; Bikram coal ramp-up to full capacity next year.
Premium and blended share target of 100% is not committed; quarter-to-quarter reversal possible as OPC demand grows in non-trade segments.
Jute business still under stress with plant shutdowns, and no strategic investor planned; policy support is awaited.
summary.management_tone: Management was guarded on forward numbers, repeatedly declining specific guidance on volume, EBITDA and blended targets citing market volatility and geopolitical uncertainty. It was confident about the strategy of premium and blended cement and capacity discipline, and about cost levers from Bikram coal and incentives. Answers on cash flow and debt were direct, while some questions on interest cost and EBITDA were deflected.
